From ca1f4d702d534387aa1f16379edb3b03cdb6ceda Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Sven Schnelle <svens@linux.ibm.com>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2021 16:08:18 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] s390: clear pt_regs::flags on irq entry

The current irq entry code doesn't initialize pt_regs::flags. On exit to
user mode arch_do_signal_or_restart() tests whether PIF_SYSCALL is set,
which might yield wrong results.

Fix this by clearing pt_regs::flags in the entry.S irq handler
code.

Reported-by: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Sven Schnelle <svens@linux.ibm.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>
Fixes: 56e62a737028 ("s390: convert to generic entry")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.12
Signed-off-by: Vasily Gorbik <gor@linux.ibm.com>

diff --git a/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S b/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
index 9cc71ca9a88f..e84f495e7eb2 100644
--- a/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
+++ b/arch/s390/kernel/entry.S
@@ -418,6 +418,7 @@ ENTRY(\name)
 	xgr	%r6,%r6
 	xgr	%r7,%r7
 	xgr	%r10,%r10
+	xc	__PT_FLAGS(8,%r11),__PT_FLAGS(%r11)
 	mvc	__PT_R8(64,%r11),__LC_SAVE_AREA_ASYNC
 	stmg	%r8,%r9,__PT_PSW(%r11)
 	tm	%r8,0x0001		# coming from user space?
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `arch/s390/kernel/entry.S`**
   - A new line of code was added to clear the `pt_regs::flags` during the IRQ entry process. Specifically, the line `xc __PT_FLAGS(8,%r11),__PT_FLAGS(%r11)` was inserted. This operation ensures that the flags are reset, preventing any incorrect behavior when the system exits to user mode.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `entry.S` addresses a bug related to the handling of `pt_regs::flags` during IRQ entry. The previous implementation did not initialize these flags, which could lead to incorrect results when checking if `PIF_SYSCALL` is set in the `arch_do_signal_or_restart()` function. By clearing the flags upon entry, the patch ensures that the system behaves correctly when transitioning from interrupt context back to user mode, thus fixing the reported issue. This change is part of a broader effort to improve the IRQ handling in the s390 architecture, as indicated by the reference to a previous commit that converted to a generic entry.

s390: clear pt_regs::flags on irq entry

The current irq entry code doesn't initialize pt_regs::flags. On exit to
user mode arch_do_signal_or_restart() tests whether PIF_SYSCALL is set,
which might yield wrong results.

Fix this by clearing pt_regs::flags in the entry.S irq handler
code.

Reported-by: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: Sven Schnelle <svens@linux.ibm.com>
Reviewed-by: Heiko Carstens <hca@linux.ibm.com>

Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org> # 5.12

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```

```
```
pt_regs::flags
```
```
PIF_SYSCALL
```
Reason:
The `pt_regs::flags` is not initialized during the IRQ entry, which means it may contain stale values. When the system checks for the `PIF_SYSCALL` flag in the `arch_do_signal_or_restart()` function, it can yield incorrect results due to these uninitialized or incorrect flag values, leading to erroneous behavior when transitioning from interrupt context to user mode.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```
xc	__PT_FLAGS(8,%r11),__PT_FLAGS(%r11)
```
Reason:
This line of code clears the `pt_regs::flags` during the IRQ entry by explicitly initializing it to a known state. This ensures that the flags do not retain stale values, allowing the `arch_do_signal_or_restart()` function to correctly assess the state of the system and the `PIF_SYSCALL` flag, thus preventing incorrect behavior during the transition from interrupt context to user mode.
